title: The dry-run review panel that tells the operator when to switch anti-rug to live selling shows only the events this browser tab happened to receive, plus hard-coded zero charts and a filter that does nothing, so "zero false positives in 7 days" cannot be read from it

evidence.note: panel headline: "7-day dry-run review window for <CHAIN>"
empty-state advice: "After 7 days with zero false positives, you can flip <CHAIN>_ANTIRUG_LIVE_EXECUTE=true in .env and restart"
detection-latency histogram counts are a constant [0, 0, 0, 0, 0] (comment: no latency field wired)
Flashbots verdict bars are a constant [0, 0, 0]
the signal-source filter returns true whatever is selected
anti-rug events exist only as received on this socket since the tab opened, capped at 100 per chain
nothing loads past events on open or reconnect
"Dry-run events today" and "Suppressed today" count only this tab's received events
the only server event list is the circuit-breaker ring buffer (bounded by circuitBreakerTriggers, default 3), not a 7-day record, and the dashboard does not call it

sibling_sites_checked: Every dashboard surface that reports anti-rug detections: FrontrunDistributionPanel (this finding), AntiRugMonitorTile counts and last-10 list (same session-only source), the per-position badge (AUD-DASH-001), the CB-reset trigger list (push payload, AUD-DASH-002). Server side: the only event read route is the ring buffer of at most circuitBreakerTriggers entries (antiRug.ts:78-96); no persisted 7-day store exists in src/api. The live-execute switch itself (per-chain ANTIRUG_LIVE_EXECUTE) and its validation are ANTIRUG-slice items (card ANTIRUG-07 for numeric settings); this entry covers only the evidence the dashboard offers for flipping it.
severity_rationale: S2 LOSS (indirect, through an operator decision): the panel instructs the operator to arm live anti-rug market sells after a week without false positives, but it cannot show any detection that happened while this tab was closed or disconnected (a reload shows "No dry-run events yet"), and two of its three charts are fixed zeros presented as data. Arming live exits on that evidence can turn false-positive detections into real sells of healthy positions. Not S1: a human decision sits between the display and any loss, and logs/Telegram dry-run alerts (exitTrigger.ts:195) are another record.
recommendation: Decide (card DASH-01) what evidence gates the live-execute switch; at least remove or label the placeholder charts and the no-op filter as not wired, and stop presenting a session-only list as a 7-day record. Real-path test: record dry-run detections with the tab closed, reopen and assert they are shown. Nothing changed in Phase 22.
